stories.title: Flock unveils a tool meant to flag police misuse of its cameras — but won't explain how it works
stories.summary: Flock, the automated license-plate-reader company facing scrutiny over officers misusing its network to track people (the so-called "stalker cop" problem), announced a new tool it says will help identify abuse. The company has not disclosed how the tool actually functions, and outside experts quoted by Ars Technica say Flock "can't tech its way out" of a problem rooted in how police use the system, not just its code. Engadget reports Flock is also making changes meant to make the cameras themselves harder for officers to misuse.
stories.whyItMatters: Flock's cameras are used widely by police departments, so how it polices misuse of its own surveillance network has broad implications for privacy and law-enforcement accountability nationwide.
whatToWatch: Whether Flock publishes technical details on how the new detection tool works
Any independent audits or third-party verification of its effectiveness
Response from police accountability advocates and lawmakers
questions: What actually triggers the tool's abuse detection?
Will Flock release usage data showing whether misuse has declined?

stories.title: Trump orders 100% tariffs on heavy and 'sensitive' drones plus all aircraft parts
stories.summary: The Trump administration declared 100 percent tariffs covering many heavy and "sensitive" drones, along with all aircraft parts, according to Engadget and The Verge. The move extends the administration's broader tariff push into aerospace and drone hardware categories.
stories.whyItMatters: A 100 percent tariff would sharply raise costs for drone makers, operators, and aviation supply chains that rely on imported components, likely accelerating a push toward domestic manufacturing or price increases passed to buyers.
whatToWatch: Which specific drone categories and countries of origin are covered
Industry and trade-partner reaction
Any exemptions carved out for commercial or agricultural drone use
questions: How is "sensitive" being defined for tariff purposes?

stories.title: Apple built a China-specific AI model with help from Alibaba
stories.summary: Apple has trained its own AI model tailored for the Chinese market, developed with assistance from Alibaba, according to The Verge. Details beyond that are limited, but it points to Apple maintaining a separate AI stack for China distinct from its global Apple Intelligence effort.
stories.whyItMatters: China's regulatory environment for AI and data has pushed Apple to build parallel infrastructure with a local partner, underscoring how geopolitics is fragmenting even Apple's tightly controlled software stack.
whatToWatch: When and how the China-specific model reaches users
Whether Apple discloses more about Alibaba's role
Any regulatory approval steps in China
questions: What capabilities will this model support versus Apple's global AI features?
How is user data handled differently under this arrangement?

stories.whyItMatters: As AI companies race to secure power, understanding why these plants pollute more heavily bears directly on the environmental cost of the data center buildout underpinning the industry's growth.

Any moves by AI companies to shift toward cleaner power commitments

stories.title: Apple proposes taking a 5-15% cut of payments made through external App Store links
stories.summary: Apple has proposed charging developers a commission of 5 to 15 percent on transactions processed outside the App Store via external payment links, according to Engadget. The move comes as Apple continues adjusting its App Store rules under ongoing legal and regulatory pressure over its payment policies.
stories.whyItMatters: Any fee Apple attaches to external payments affects how much relief developers actually get from being allowed to route around Apple's in-app purchase system, shaping the real-world impact of antitrust rulings against Apple.
whatToWatch: Developer reaction to the proposed commission rates
Whether courts or regulators deem the new rate acceptable compliance
Any further adjustments from Apple
questions: How does this rate compare to Apple's standard in-app purchase commission?
Will regulators consider 5-15% sufficient to satisfy prior rulings?

stories.title: Judge orders Google to make it easier to install rival Android app stores
stories.summary: A judge overseeing the Epic v. Google antitrust case ordered Google to reduce friction around installing rival app stores on Android devices, reportedly telling the company "that is not acceptable" regarding its current approach, per The Verge.
stories.whyItMatters: The ruling could meaningfully reshape how Android app distribution works, forcing Google to open the platform to competitors in ways it has resisted, with implications for app store competition broadly.
whatToWatch: Google's compliance timeline and specific changes made
Whether Google appeals the order
Impact on rival app store adoption
questions: What specific installation steps does Google need to change?
Will this affect Google's Play Store fees or policies more broadly?

stories.title: Take Apple's spyware attack notifications seriously, TechCrunch warns
stories.summary: TechCrunch is urging users who receive an Apple push notification warning of a spyware attack to treat it seriously, rather than dismiss it as a false alarm. Apple periodically sends such threat notifications to targets of suspected state-sponsored or mercenary spyware.
stories.whyItMatters: Targeted spyware campaigns continue to threaten journalists, activists, and other high-risk individuals, and Apple's warnings are one of the few direct signals victims get that they've been targeted.
whatToWatch: Whether Apple or researchers disclose which spyware vendor or campaign prompted the advisory
Any follow-up security guidance from Apple
questions: What should a recipient concretely do after getting such a notification?
